newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on Cenbank repos.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on Cenbank repos.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 60 basis points at 23.40 percent on Tuesday after the central bank agreed to set two repurchase agreements in the secondary market for 200 million pesos each, traders said.
Dealers said the repurchase agreements were both assigned at 16 days, and at rates of 23.91 percent and 23.00 percent.
"The market was under pressure for most of the day from high secondary auction rates assigned yesterday when it drained liquidity," a trader said.
"Nonetheless, pressure eased when Banco de Mexico announced it had purchased paper through repos," he added.
Another trader said the central bank decided to withdraw paper from the system to offset upside pressure on rates from draining hefty amounts of liquidity from the system.
"The aim is to soothe the market because they are draining liquidity," he said.
The central bank had earlier announced it was to drain 6.632 billion pesos from the system through eight secondary auctions, which it assigned at rates of between 25.15-25.92 percent.
Traders lowered their estimates of predicted hikes in bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at the central bank's weekly auction later in the day after the central bank withdrew paper.
Nonetheless, several dealers declined to forecast results for the primary auction, saying a volatile secondary market made error margins too wide.
"The market is very odd, what is happening is sheer speculation and besides, Banco de Mexico has handled secondary auctions very badly," a trader said.
"The 28.70 percent they assigned at yesterday was unbelievable and today they drained at 23.00 percent... I just don't understand what Banco de Mexico or the market is up to," he added.
The Interacciones brokerage said in a report Banco de Mexico could be raising secondary rates in order to contain an unexpected rise in the monetary base.

A Reuters survey nN15565072 of money market traders showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would place bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average rate of 23.16 percent. This would represent an increase of 83 basis points since last week.
Auction results are due to be announced at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 60 basis points at 25.90 percent.
On the Cetes futures market in Chicago, June contracts closed up 47 centavos at 77.80 pesos.
Liquidity of 6.917 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
